headline: Bitcoin fell below $60,000 at the US open as more than $1 billion of bets on rising prices were wiped out, Anthropic's shares slid on day two, and a House crypto tax bill may get a vote before Congress ends.

stories.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 at the US open as more than $1 billion of rising-price bets are wiped out
stories.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 around the US stock market open on Friday, down from an overnight low near $61,200. Traders who had borrowed to bet on higher prices were forced out in large numbers, and big funds kept pulling money from bitcoin ETFs. When forced selling and fund outflows hit together, prices can fall faster than the news alone would suggest.
points: Bitcoin fell to $59,950 on Bitstamp and traded around $60,000 at about 15:45 UTC, per CryptoPotato.
More than $340 million of long (rising-price) bets were liquidated in one hour and $1.01 billion in a day, with more than 225,000 traders liquidated, per CryptoPotato citing CoinGlass.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of $582.2 million on 19 Nov, about $541.1 million of it from BlackRock's IBIT; November outflows are nearing $3.5 billion, per The Block.
US two-year real interest rates rose above 2.40%, the highest since 2023, and gold fell nearly 3%, per CoinDesk; higher rates make assets that pay no interest less attractive.

stories.title: Anthropic shares slide on their second day, after crypto versions of the stock pointed lower overnight
stories.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 and closed its first Nasdaq day at $97.17. On Friday the shares fell about 9%, leaving them only a few percent above the IPO price. Crypto-based contracts that track the stock trade around the clock and had already signalled a lower price during Asian hours. A token or contract that follows a stock is not the same as owning the stock.
points: Anthropic shares fell 9% on day two, per Yahoo Finance (14:40 UTC).
Hyperliquid's ANT perpetual contract traded in the low $90s in Asian hours, below the first-day close, per CoinDesk.
Ark Invest bought 934,968 Anthropic shares, about $90.9 million, on debut, and trimmed its Ethereum and Solana staking ETF holdings, per The Block.
The CoinDesk 20 index fell 1.9% with none of its members higher, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: A House crypto tax bill could get a vote before this Congress ends
stories.summary: Rep. Steven Horsford said he wants a House vote on the bipartisan Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act before this Congress ends, and that Ways and Means Chair Jason Smith agreed the chance exists. No vote date has been set. Of the crypto bills in Washington, this is the one most likely to change how everyday users fill in their taxes.
points: The bill cleared the House Ways and Means Committee 38-5 in September, per The Block.
Using crypto to pay fees of $10 or less would not need to be reported as a gain or loss, per The Block.
Wash-sale rules would extend to crypto, so selling at a loss and buying straight back would no longer let you claim the loss, per The Block.
Mining and staking rewards would be taxed as ordinary income, per The Block.

briefs.title: Death Bets Act heads to the House
briefs.summary: The Senate passed S.4035, which would ban prediction-market contracts on death, terrorism, assassination and war; it now goes to the House, per The Block.

briefs.title: Coinbase plans its own prediction contracts
briefs.summary: Coinbase is targeting its own US prediction contracts in the first half of 2027; its prediction business passed $200 million in annualized revenue in Q3, per Decrypt.

briefs.title: Ether funds keep losing money
briefs.summary: US spot ether ETFs had net outflows of $131.2 million on 19 Nov, per The Block.

briefs.title: Altcoins fall harder than bitcoin
briefs.summary: Within the CoinDesk 20, Zcash fell 11%, NEAR 9.3% and HYPE 7%, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: CFTC chair on Hyperliquid and US users
briefs.summary: CFTC Chair Selig said on-chain venues like Hyperliquid can reach US retail users by registering as an exchange or partnering with a registered one, per The Block.

briefs.title: Banks push back on tokenized copies of their shares
briefs.summary: JPMorgan, Goldman and Wells Fargo object to third-party tokenized versions of their shares, and Wintermute's policy chief said the crypto lobby must "clean house a little bit", per The Block.

briefs.title: Lagarde warns on tokenized finance
briefs.summary: ECB President Lagarde warned Europe could lose its lead in tokenized finance without common rules, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Ripple's legal chief on who sets crypto rules
briefs.summary: Ripple CLO Stuart Alderoty expects the SEC, CFTC and OCC, not a broad Clarity Act, to lead crypto policy, per The Block.
